title: Enriched small-object factorization for a tensor-compatible weak factorization system
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. Let $\mathcal C$ be a category enriched over $\mathcal U$-small simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], with associative simplicial composition and identity vertices, and underlying morphisms the vertices of its mapping sets. Suppose $\mathcal C$ has small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and small limits (colimits in its opposite category), is tensored and cotensored over simplicial sets, and is locally presentable: for some infinite regular $\kappa$, a small set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve $\kappa$-filtered colimits generates $\mathcal C$ under such colimits. Here regular means a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of size less than $\kappa$ has size less than $\kappa$, and $\kappa$-filtered means that every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms admits a cocone. Tensors $K\otimes X$ and cotensors $Y^K$ satisfy the enriched natural adjunctions
$$\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(K\otimes X,Y)\cong\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(K,\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,Y))\cong\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,Y^K).$$
Let $J$ be a small set of morphisms of $\mathcal C$, let $R$ be the class with the ordinary right lifting property against $J$, and let $L$ be the class with the ordinary left lifting property against $R$. Lifting means existence of a diagonal filler in every commutative square with the indicated left and right maps. Assume that $K\otimes j$ belongs to $L$ for every $j\in J$ and every small simplicial set $K$. Let $\operatorname{Arr}_{\Delta}(\mathcal C)$ be the simplicial arrow category, with mapping set from $u:X\to Y$ to $v:X'\to Y'$ the equalizer imposing $vb=cu$ on pairs $(b,c)\in\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,X')\times\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(Y,Y')$. There exists a simplicial functor $E:\operatorname{Arr}_{\Delta}(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal C$ and simplicially enriched natural transformations giving, for every $u:X\to Y$, a factorization
$$X\xrightarrow{i_u}E(u)\xrightarrow{p_u}Y,\qquad p_ui_u=u,\quad i_u\in L,\quad p_u\in R.$$
Here a simplicial functor assigns objects and simplicial maps of mapping sets preserving composition and identities; an enriched natural transformation has component vertices whose naturality equations hold as equalities of simplicial maps. Thus enriched naturality includes all simplicial parameters of commutative squares. No model category structure on $\mathcal C$ is assumed.

source.place: Categorical Homotopy Theory, Theorem 13.2.1 and its proof, pp.177-178 (PDF pp.193-194), with enriched arrow category in section 13.1 and the tensor condition preceding Corollary 13.2.4. Specialized to simplicial enrichment and locally presentable underlying categories, which permit the small-object argument. This is the generic enriched small-object input used in HTT Example A.3.4.4 and Lemma A.3.4.15. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this enriched theorem. Theorem 12.5.1, hypothesis (*), supplies the locally presentable small-object case; the paragraph ending section 13.1 explains enriched bicompleteness from the stated limits and tensors.

proof.text:
Ordinary colimits here have an enriched universal property. For a small diagram $D$, any $T$, and every $n\geq0$, the given cotensor adjunction and the ordinary colimit universal property give
$$\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(\operatorname{colim}D,T)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{colim}D,T^{\Delta[n]})=\lim_a\operatorname{Hom}(D_a,T^{\Delta[n]})=(\lim_a\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(D_a,T))_n.$$
The maps are induced by the colimit injections; naturality of the adjunction makes these bijections commute with every simplicial operator. Thus they are isomorphisms of simplicial sets, including for empty diagrams. Moreover $K\otimes-$ preserves these ordinary colimits: its ordinary right adjoint is $(-)^K$, so maps from $K\otimes\operatorname{colim}D$ to $T$ are exactly compatible maps $K\otimes D_a\to T$. This is a direct application of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and the adjunctions in the statement; full weighted bicompleteness is unnecessary.

source.place: Theorem 7.5.3 and its dual, printed pp.90-91 (PDF pp.105-106); section 13.1, printed p.176 (PDF p.191).

proof.text: Pointwise colimits of enriched diagrams are enriched functors. Explicitly, suppose $F_a$ are simplicial functors on a simplicial category $\mathcal A$ and the diagram maps are enriched natural. Put $F(x)=\operatorname{colim}_aF_a(x)$. For $H=\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal A}(x,y)$, the actions $H\otimes F_a(x)\to F_a(y)\to F(y)$ are compatible. Step 1 gives a unique action $H\otimes F(x)\to F(y)$, hence a simplicial map $H\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(F(x),F(y))$. Identity and composition equations hold after precomposition with each colimit injection, where they are the equations for $F_a$; the colimit universal property gives the equations on $F$. Any compatible family of enriched natural maps out of the diagram induces an enriched natural map out of $F$ by the identical injection test. This proves, in particular, enriched functoriality of the coproducts, pushouts and ordinal colimits used below.

source.place: Section 13.1, last paragraph; section 13.2, proof after diagram (13.2.2): conical colimits give enriched functors.

proof.text:
For $j:A_j\to B_j$ set $S_j(f)=\operatorname{Sq}(j,f)$, the mapping simplicial set in the arrow category from the statement. It is small, being a degreewise equalizer of products of small mapping sets. Composition defines $\operatorname{Sq}(f,g)\times S_j(f)\to S_j(g)$ by $(h,s)\mapsto h\circ s$. Tensor adjunction makes $f\mapsto S_j(f)\otimes A_j$ and $f\mapsto S_j(f)\otimes B_j$ enriched functors: for a parameter $H=\operatorname{Sq}(f,g)$ their actions are the maps
$$H\otimes(S_j(f)\otimes A_j)\cong(H\times S_j(f))\otimes A_j\longrightarrow S_j(g)\otimes A_j,$$
and the displayed formula with $B_j$. The associativity isomorphism follows by applying the tensor adjunction twice. The action equations are the associativity and unit equations of composition. Projection of a square onto its two components and evaluation give enriched natural maps $S_j(f)\otimes A_j\to\operatorname{dom}f$ and $S_j(f)\otimes B_j\to\operatorname{cod}f$; their square commutes because $s$ satisfies the defining equalizer equation. Their naturality is $(h\circ s)_0=h_0\circ s_0$, $(h\circ s)_1=h_1\circ s_1$, as equalities of simplicial maps.

source.place: Section 13.1, equation (13.1.1) and Remark 13.1.2; section 13.2, formula for L_0.

proof.text: For $f:X\to Y$ form $P(f)=\coprod_{j\in J}S_j(f)\otimes A_j$ and $Q(f)=\coprod_{j\in J}S_j(f)\otimes B_j$. The maps from step 3 give a square from $a_f:P(f)\to Q(f)$ to $f$. Let $V(f)=X\amalg_{P(f)}Q(f)$, let $c_f:X\to V(f)$ be its injection and $r_f:V(f)\to Y$ its induced map, so $r_fc_f=f$. By step 2 all these assignments are enriched functors or enriched natural transformations. More explicitly, an $H$-parameterized square $f\to g$ gives maps $H\otimes X\to X'\to V(g)$ and $H\otimes Q(f)\to Q(g)\to V(g)$ agreeing on $H\otimes P(f)$ by step 3. Since $H\otimes-$ preserves the pushout, they induce $H\otimes V(f)\to V(g)$. Its equations on the two pushout injections give $V(h)c_f=c_g h_0$ and $r_gV(h)=h_1r_f$ with the same parameter $H$. Identity and composition follow from those equations on both injections.

For each $j\in J$, [lem-coef-object-presentability-rank] gives an infinite regular $\tau_j\in\mathcal U$ for which $\operatorname{Hom}(A_j,-)$ preserves small $\tau_j$-filtered colimits. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to the family of sets of ordinals below $\tau_j$. Obtain an infinite regular $\lambda\in\mathcal U$ greater than the cardinality of their disjoint union, hence greater than every $\tau_j$. This also works when $J$ is empty. Regard $\lambda$ as its initial ordinal. It is a nonzero limit ordinal, and its category of predecessors is $\tau_j$-filtered for every $j$: a set of fewer than $\tau_j$ ordinals below $\lambda$ has supremum below $\lambda$ by regularity, providing the cocone (use $0$ for an empty diagram). This choice of $\lambda$ is independent of $f$.

source.place: Section 13.2, smallness convention referring to Theorem 12.2.2; replace the compact-domain countable notation by a uniform regular ordinal using the existing presentability and cardinal-bound leaves.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-transfinite-recursion] up to $\lambda$, choosing the colimits of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] once. The records at stage $\alpha$ consist of enriched functors $Z_\alpha$ on the arrow category, enriched maps $p_\alpha:Z_\alpha\to\operatorname{cod}$, and enriched transition maps $t_{\alpha\beta}$, with $t_{\alpha\alpha}=1$, $t_{\beta\gamma}t_{\alpha\beta}=t_{\alpha\gamma}$ and $p_\beta t_{\alpha\beta}=p_\alpha$. At zero take $Z_0(f)=X$ and $p_0(f)=f$. At a successor apply step 4 to $p_\alpha(f)$: put $Z_{\alpha+1}(f)=V(p_\alpha(f))$, $p_{\alpha+1}(f)=r_{p_\alpha(f)}$, $t_{\alpha,\alpha+1}=c_{p_\alpha(f)}$, and compose this transition with the earlier ones. The assignment $f\mapsto p_\alpha(f)$ is enriched as an arrow-valued functor because $p_\alpha$ is enriched natural; hence the successor records are enriched by step 4. At a nonzero limit $\beta\leq\lambda$, take $Z_\beta(f)=\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\beta}Z_\alpha(f)$ with its injections as transitions; the compatible $p_\alpha(f)$ induce $p_\beta(f)$. Step 2 proves enrichment of these records. At successors the invariant follows from $r_qc_q=q$; at limits it follows on every injection by the cocone equations and uniqueness. This is a total recursion rule by assigning a dummy record to an incoherent input prefix; well-order induction using the checks just given shows that the actual prefixes are coherent and never receive the dummy. All colimit shapes and attaching sets are $\mathcal U$-small. Set $E=Z_\lambda$, $i=t_{0\lambda}$ and $p=p_\lambda$; the invariant gives $pi=f$.

source.place: Section 13.2, Quillen construction in the final proof paragraph, printed pp.177-178 (PDF pp.192-193), with the transfinite iteration of Theorem 12.2.2 instead of the compact-domain countable illustration.

proof.text: Each summand $S_j(q)\otimes j$ of $a_q$ is in $L$ by the item hypothesis, since $S_j(q)$ is small. Their coproduct is in $L$: for any $r\in R$ and square from that coproduct to $r$, restrict to each summand, choose a filler there, and combine the fillers by the coproduct universal property. By pushout stability in [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], every $c_q$ lies in $L$. The chain of step 6 is continuous at every nonzero limit, so [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting], with $T=R$ and $\theta=\lambda$, puts $i_f=t_{0\lambda}(f)$ in $L$. No assertion that the maps $S_j(q)\otimes j$ are themselves $J$-cellular is used.

source.place: Section 13.2, hypothesis (star) and proof invoking Lemma 11.1.4; transfinite version of the left-class argument.

proof.text: Fix $j:A_j\to B_j$ and an ordinary square $a:A_j\to E(f)$, $b:B_j\to Y$ with $p_fa=bj$. By step 5, $\operatorname{Hom}(A_j,-)$ preserves the colimit $E(f)=\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\lambda}Z_\alpha(f)$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] gives $\alpha<\lambda$ and $a_\alpha:A_j\to Z_\alpha(f)$ with $t_{\alpha\lambda}a_\alpha=a$. Then $p_\alpha a_\alpha=p_ft_{\alpha\lambda}a_\alpha=bj$, so $(a_\alpha,b)$ is a vertex of $S_j(p_\alpha(f))$. This requires no presentability of $B_j$ and no descent of an equality to a later stage: the codomain is the fixed $Y$ throughout.

source.place: Section 13.2, final lifting argument, printed p.178 (PDF p.193), applied after the regular-ordinal smallness bound.

proof.text: Tensor the vertex $\Delta[0]\to S_j(p_\alpha(f))$ with $B_j$, using $\Delta[0]\otimes B_j\cong B_j$, and include its image in $Q(p_\alpha(f))$. Its composite with the pushout injection is $d:B_j\to Z_{\alpha+1}(f)$. The pushout equation and evaluation at this vertex give $dj=t_{\alpha,\alpha+1}a_\alpha$ and $p_{\alpha+1}d=b$. Thus $h=t_{\alpha+1,\lambda}d$ satisfies $hj=a$ and $p_fh=b$. Here $\alpha+1<\lambda$ because $\lambda$ is a limit ordinal. Every square for every $j$ has this filler, so $p_f\in J^\square=R$.

source.place: Remark 13.1.2 and section 13.2, last diagram and following paragraph, printed pp.176-178 (PDF pp.191-193).

proof.text: The enriched recursion supplies simplicial maps $\operatorname{Sq}(f,g)\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(E(f),E(g))$ preserving identities and composition, and enriched naturality of $i$ and $p$. In particular, on an $n$-simplex $(b,c)$ with $gb=cf$, these maps satisfy $E(b,c)i_f=i_gb$ and $p_gE(b,c)=cp_f$ as equalities of $n$-simplices. They commute with all face and degeneracy maps by construction, which is exactly the asserted enriched naturality. Together with $p_fi_f=f$, step 7 and step 9, these are all parts of the conclusion. For $J=\varnothing$, every $P(q)$ and $Q(q)$ is initial; choosing the canonical pushouts gives $Z_\alpha(f)=X$ throughout, hence $i_f=1_X$ and $p_f=f$. Empty tensors and empty colimits require no exception to any step.

source.place: Section 13.1 arrow enrichment and section 13.2 conclusion; explicit unpacking of the constructed enriched factorization.
